verdicts.reviewer_notes: Fetched the only cited source (whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/09/inaugurating-the-era-of-super-intelligence/) four times on 2026-10-07. Extraction was inconsistent. Fetch 1 returned a paraphrase that left out 'to the maximum extent permitted by law' and 'non-statutory documents', and gave sec. 3(b) as 'assess whether modifications to existing statutory references are necessary'. Fetches 2, 3 and 4 returned consistent verbatim text, which I rely on. CONFIRMED: the page shows 'Executive Order 14434', the title, and the date September 29, 2026 (header and signature block). Sec. 2(a), verbatim: 'To the maximum extent permitted by law, executive departments and agencies (agencies) shall use "Super Intelligence" and "SI" in place of "Artificial Intelligence" and "AI" in official correspondence, public communications, websites, reports, policy documents, and other non-statutory documents within the executive branch.' Sec. 2(b): nothing requires alteration of previously issued regulations, Presidential actions, contracts, grants, or other historical documents. Sec. 3(a): the terms mean the technologies and systems encompassed by 'artificial intelligence' as defined in 15 U.S.C. 9401(3). Sec. 3(b): 'Within 60 days of the date of this order, the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology (APST) ... shall submit to the President proposed legislative language to establish a Federal definition of "Super Intelligence" and "SI"'. Three fetches confirm the 60-day deadline. A string search found 'preempt' absent, and 'State' appears only in an image caption ('The White House State Ballroom Interior View'), so 'does not address preemption of state law' is supported. Sec. 4 says the order creates no enforceable right or benefit, which supports 'no obligations for private parties on its face'. Stage in_force fits an EO signed 29 Sept 2026. The page states no separate effective date ('effective' is absent). No duplicate exists in content/items or content/instruments (grep for 14434, super-intelligence and Super Intelligence found nothing outside runs/). Tone is neutral. PROBLEM: the conforming-amendments wording overstates the order. Sec. 3(b)(ii), verbatim from fetch 3 and confirmed by the string search in fetch 4, reads: 'any proposed conforming amendments, as appropriate, to existing statutory references to "artificial intelligence" and "AI"'. The item says the APST is to submit legislative language 'and conforming amendments', which reads as mandatory, while the order makes them conditional ('any', 'as appropriate'). The item also omits that the proposal must include (i) an assessment of whether the new definition should modify, expand upon or supersede the existing statutory definition, and (iii) recommendations for further executive action. Those omissions are acceptable, but the qualifier must be restored. Minor point, no change required: type 'regulation' is an imperfect fit for an executive order, but ITEM_TYPES has no executive-order value.
required_changes: In summary, replace 'Within 60 days the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology is to submit proposed legislative language for a federal definition of 'Super Intelligence' and conforming amendments.' with: 'Within 60 days the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology is to submit to the President proposed legislative language for a federal definition of 'Super Intelligence' and 'SI', including an assessment of whether it should modify or supersede the existing statutory definition of 'artificial intelligence' and any conforming amendments to existing statutory references, as appropriate.'

verdicts.reviewer_notes: Read the full signed PDF (gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/FINAL-N-9-26-AI-EO-9.18.26-SIGNED.pdf, 3 pages) on 2026-10-07. WebFetch could not extract it, so I read the saved PDF directly. CONFIRMED against the order text: issued 'to become effective immediately', and the signature block says '18th day of September 2026', so the timeline date 2026-09-18, stage in_force and kind executive_order are correct. Para. 1: by May 1, 2027, GovOps shall 'complete the requirements of Section 8898.1 of the Government Code and develop application requirements, procedures, and criteria for independent verification organizations and publicly post them'. Para. 2: by December 1, 2027, GovOps shall 'complete the requirements of subdivision (a) of Section 11549.82 ... and begin taking the actions required by subdivision (b)'. Para. 3: GovOps, in consultation with Cal OES, shall by November 16, 2026 submit to the Governor's office recommendations 'developed in consultation with national experts, addressing the technical feasibility and potential efficacy of amendments to existing state laws regarding AI safety and security', covering at least (a) onsite IVOs at all large frontier developers, (b) independent verification of safety frameworks, transparency reports and risk assessments, (c) a 'kill switch' verified on an ongoing basis by an IVO, and (d) updating the critical safety incident definition 'to include a range of loss-of-control incidents'. The no-enforceable-rights clause is present. The summary's 'technical feasibility and potential efficacy' phrasing is the order's own, not the press release's. The 23 Sept release instead says 'accelerate the implementation timelines for SB 813 and AB 1405' and 'recommendations for potential changes to further strengthen state law'. The publisher is the issuing office, so the primary tier is correct. No duplicate in content/items or content/instruments (grep for N-9-26 found nothing outside runs/). PROBLEMS: (1) The summary calls both sections 'California's independent verification organization provisions (Gov. Code 8898.1 ...; 11549.82 ...)'. The order ties only 8898.1 to independent verification organizations and never says what 11549.82 covers. The 23 Sept release refers to two bills, SB 813 and AB 1405, and the preamble separately mentions regulating AI auditors, so 11549.82 may be a different regime. I could not check the code text because leginfo.legislature.ca.gov returned 403. (2) The summary's '11549.82 by 1 December 2027' overstates the order: only subdivision (a) must be completed by that date, and subdivision (b) actions need only begin. The key_obligations entry gets this right, but the summary does not. (3) The key_obligations wording 'broader critical safety incident definitions' paraphrases the order loosely. The order says 'updating the definition of critical safety incidents ... to include a range of loss-of-control incidents'.
required_changes: In summary, replace 'sets deadlines for the Government Operations Agency to implement California's independent verification organization provisions (Gov. Code 8898.1 by 1 May 2027; 11549.82 by 1 December 2027)' with: 'directs the Government Operations Agency to complete the requirements of Gov. Code 8898.1, including posting application requirements and criteria for independent verification organizations, by 1 May 2027, and to complete subdivision (a) of Gov. Code 11549.82 and begin the actions required by subdivision (b) by 1 December 2027'. Do not describe 11549.82 as an independent verification organization provision unless a fetched primary source shows that.
In key_obligations[2], replace 'broader critical safety incident definitions' with 'updating the definition of critical safety incidents to include a range of loss-of-control incidents'.
